title: Define inter-team acceptance checkpoints and handoff playbook for Private deployment scope changes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope: When PRD scope changes are proposed for the Private deployment path (RBAC changes, KMS integration, or migration windows), we need a lightweight, repeatable set of inter-team checkpoints and a handoff playbook so Engineering, Design, and Legal sign off with clear acceptance criteria. This ticket clarifies the exact artifacts each team must produce, the order of signoffs, acceptable fallbacks, and escalation paths.

Why now: Recent scope changes to the Private upgrade PRD increased risk of rollout delays because legal approval and console UX decisions arrived after engineering completed work. We need deterministic gates to keep schedules and SLAs predictable.
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical PRD section titled 'Inter-team Acceptance Checklist' exists and is linked from the root PRD
Engineering provides an implementation intent doc (1-2 pages) that maps changes to runtime, upgrade path, and migration risks
Design supplies console mockups and microcopy for any new/reused flows; handoff spec includes accessibility notes
Legal signs a short checklist confirming data residency, contractual change notes, and any export-control flags (or explicitly documents an open risk)
Each acceptance item has an owner and a deadlines annotation; all items marked 'required' must be cleared before the release branch is cut
Fallback plan(s) for partial rollouts are documented and tested (canary/abort criteria are defined)
A roll-forward/roll-back runbook is created and reviewed by SRE/Engineering and marked 'reviewed' in the PRD

risks_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: delaying legal signoff until full dataflow is complete reduces speed-to-release but minimizes contract risk.
Risk: partial UI decisions made after engineering work may require rework of console APIs and add ~2 sprint overhead.
Mitigation: freeze API contract lines in the PRD prior to engineering implementation; allow UI microcopy to iterate until signoff with feature flag gating.
